scope_note: Questions are grounded in the Huang-Shen 2021 IMEX-BDFk/SAV scheme for periodic incompressible Navier-Stokes and remain genuinely open after this replication. They are not merely 'things we didn't run' - each identifies a place where the paper's setting, the SAV mechanism, or the pressure-Poisson consistency has an untested or under-specified edge.

questions.q: How should the SAV auxiliary-variable r-update be modified when an external forcing f is present, so that the discrete dissipation law remains energy-consistent with E(u)=1/2||grad u||^2 (2D) or E(u)=1/2||u||^2 (3D)?
questions.basis: Huang & Shen prove Theorem 1 (unconditional energy stability) for the unforced case f=0. Example 1 is manufactured and therefore forced, and the paper does not spell out the r-update in the forced case. Our replication had to derive (f,-Delta bar u) = (grad f, grad bar u) as the energy-consistent production term; without it the SAV factor eta starves and the solution collapses (failure_analysis.md). This works but is our design decision, not a paper-quoted equation, and the theoretical justification (which functional form of the production term preserves the discrete inequality at each BDFk order) is not written down anywhere we could find.
next_steps: Derive the r-update for the forced NS SAV system directly from the continuous dissipation identity d/dt E(u) = -nu ||nabla^2 u||^2 + (f, -Delta u) and verify it discretely for BDF1..BDF4.
Prove a modified unconditional-stability result of the form r^{n+1} <= r^n + Delta t * C(f) with an explicit forcing-dependent constant.
Numerically stress-test at very large Delta t (say Delta t >= 0.5) with a strongly forced problem to see whether the derived production term still keeps eta bounded away from 0.

questions.q: Do the fitted order-k temporal convergence rates persist for the third-order (k=3) and fourth-order (k=4) SAV/BDFk schemes when a proper 2/3-rule (or smooth Hou-Li) dealiasing filter is applied and the flow is only marginally resolved in space?
questions.basis: Our replication used N=40 Fourier modes per direction on a very smooth manufactured solution, so the spatial error is negligible and aliasing is not stressed. Huang & Shen's Fourier-Galerkin proof cleanly separates space and time, but the practical high-order IMEX+AB-k extrapolation of a quadratic nonlinearity is well known to interact with aliasing errors. Whether the 4.14 velocity order and 4.08 pressure order we recovered survive under weaker spatial resolution + explicit dealiasing is not tested here and is not addressed in the paper's Example 1.
next_steps: Sweep N in {16, 24, 32, 40} both with no dealiasing and with 2/3-rule dealiasing on the same manufactured problem.
Report fitted order-in-time as a function of N for BDF3/BDF4 to detect any order-reduction from aliasing.
Repeat with a less smooth solution (e.g. one whose Fourier tail decays only algebraically) to see if the observed order is spatial-resolution-limited before it is temporal-order-limited.

questions.q: How consistent is the recovered pressure at the discrete level - i.e. does the pressure-Poisson equation -Delta p = nabla . ( (u.nabla) u ) - nabla . f, solved on the same Fourier grid, remain LBB-clean and free of spurious modes when the SAV factor eta departs measurably from 1 (as it must at very large Delta t or under-resolved flow)?
questions.basis: In our smooth Example 1 the SAV factor eta stayed in [0.9850, 1.0008], so pressure recovery reproduced the exact pressure to 2.5e-13 and the pressure order (0.95/1.95/3.01/4.08) matched the velocity order. But the paper's Theorem 1 does not constrain how far eta can drift from 1 in stressed regimes, and the periodic pressure-Poisson consistency was checked here only in the eta ~ 1 regime. Whether pressure convergence order degrades before velocity order does when eta is genuinely non-trivial is genuinely open.
next_steps: Force eta noticeably away from 1 by (a) driving the flow much harder, (b) using coarser spatial resolution, or (c) initializing r away from E(u)+1, and monitor pressure H^1 error and its fitted order.
Compare pressure recovered from bar u vs pressure recovered from u = eta * bar u to isolate where any degradation enters.
Cross-check against a projection-method (Chorin-Temam) baseline on the same manufactured problem to bound how much of any degradation is intrinsic to periodic pressure recovery vs SAV-specific.

questions.q: Do the unconditional energy stability and order-k convergence carry over cleanly when the SAV/BDFk scheme is extended to variable-density or two-phase incompressible flow (e.g. Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes with a phase field), where the pressure-elimination trick via Leray projection no longer diagonalizes and E(u) must be augmented by an interfacial free-energy term?
questions.basis: Huang & Shen's construction leans crucially on (i) periodic BCs so pressure can be eliminated via the Leray projection, and (ii) a single kinetic-energy-based auxiliary variable r = E(u)+1. Variable-density or multiphase incompressible flow adds a density-weighted momentum equation and a phase-field free energy, and pressure elimination becomes non-diagonal (or requires a variable-coefficient Poisson solve). Whether Theorem-1-style unconditional stability and the observed order-k temporal convergence survive this extension - and, if so, what the correct SAV auxiliary variable is (single scalar vs coupled scalars for kinetic + interfacial energy) - is not addressed and not obvious.
next_steps: Formulate the analogous SAV/BDFk scheme for CHNS with r = E_kin(u) + E_int(phi) + C, and derive the discrete dissipation identity.
Rerun a manufactured-solution convergence sweep on a variable-density benchmark (e.g. Rayleigh-Taylor at moderate Atwood number) at BDF2 and BDF3 and check the fitted temporal orders.
Compare against the recent literature (Shen-Xu-Yang gPAV, and Yang-Ju IEQ-based multiphase schemes) to see whether the unconditional-stability constant blows up with the density ratio.

questions.q: Are the observed high-order (BDF3, BDF4) SAV convergence rates robust to non-periodic boundary conditions - specifically no-slip on a bounded Lipschitz domain - once the Leray-projection pressure elimination is replaced by a pressure-Poisson solve with a consistent Neumann boundary condition?
questions.basis: The paper is explicitly restricted to periodic BCs precisely because the Leray projection is then diagonal in Fourier space and pressure can be eliminated exactly. In practice most engineering incompressible-NS solvers face no-slip walls where the pressure-Poisson BC is a non-trivial choice (consistent Neumann derived from the momentum equation vs. simple zero-normal-gradient) and the projection step commutes only approximately with time discretization. Whether SAV/BDFk still delivers its full order-k in H^1 for velocity and pressure in the no-slip case - and whether Theorem 1 still yields unconditional stability with the same r-update - is left open by the paper and by this replication.
next_steps: Reformulate the SAV/BDFk scheme with a spectral-element or high-order FEM spatial discretization on a bounded domain with no-slip walls; use a consistent Neumann pressure BC.
Run the Taylor-Green-in-a-box or Kovasznay-flow manufactured test at BDF1..BDF4 and measure fitted orders in H^1.
Check whether Theorem-1-style unconditional stability requires modifying r to include a boundary-flux term (or fails outright) when u | boundary != 0 in the transient.
